findings: Physical damage is an actual deterministic update setting address i opposite to the retained program bit. Controller and code are unchanged.
potential_finite is derived from the existing finite 0/1 physical potential and finite mismatch penalty.
carrier_iff_program derives both the real program-specific recovery condition (via the existing actual expected-hitting source) and finite potential. It is not assumed as a success field.
actual_fault_envelope follows from retained code and the proved carrier characterization. No hF premise remains in its signature.
actual_fault_outside_target shows genuine damage to the original target for every source-bit-consistent input.
assembled_enters_actual_fault_system directly calls existing compiled_enters_p5 with the derived hF and himpl.
scope_limits: Protected-code physical fault class only; arbitrary program/controller corruption is not demonstrated.
The final theorem proves entry into the existing repairable carrier, not continued membership in the legitimate target for all hazard rates. Epsilon1 remains permitted by that carrier statement.
The source uses a retained target program; it does not discover/synthesize that program from the physical state.
Physical-state disturbance is deterministically opposite to the retained target, not necessarily a flip of an already-damaged current bit. Header wording should use that precise description.
No long-run resource/hazard balance or whole organizational closure is inferred.
